comment: Bytes, measured over the development build in dist/ — unminified, which is the stricter of the two and the one `npm run gates` has already produced. Source maps are excluded: they are absent from a production build and are not distributed. A budget here moves DOWN only (AGENTS.md section 11, ADR-0003 decision 5); raising one is a commit that says why, inside the diff the reviewer reads. || MEASURED. Set on 2026-09-13 from a development build at main.cjs 2173, preload.cjs 1402, renderer.js 1215, index.html 898, renderer.css 1313 — total 7001. The budget above these was set against 15 454, of which 8469 bytes were frozen contract constants that neither the preload nor the renderer reads: both entry points import the barrel, and `Object.freeze({...})` is a call expression esbuild cannot prove free of side effects, so every constant reachable through the barrel was retained. A `/* @__PURE__ */` annotation on each frozen constant lets esbuild drop the call when its result is unused, and those modules left both bundles. || MARGIN. Each budget is its measured size plus one kibibyte, rounded up to the next whole kibibyte, so the real margin is between 1024 and 2047 bytes per file. It is sized against documentation and not against code, because the development build keeps doc comments. The two bounds it sits between are both measured: the smallest thing this budget should catch is one frozen contract constant coming back, and the smallest of the four was FailureKind at 471 bytes of the renderer; the largest ordinary edit it should absorb is a doc block, and the largest single one in the project is RowFlag's clip-bit documentation at 1748 source bytes. Those two overlap, so no margin satisfies both and this one is set towards the doc block: it absorbs any ordinary doc comment several times over, it absorbs even RowFlag's on main.cjs and renderer.js though not on preload.cjs, and it does NOT catch one small constant leaking back on its own. What it does catch is the failure it was set after — the contract ring returning to the renderer entire, which cost 4634 bytes. A gate that fired on good prose would be the worse error, because src/contracts/ is where this project puts its most load-bearing prose. || TOTAL. The five budgets sum to 15 360 and the total is set below that sum deliberately, so the distributable as a whole is a second constraint and not merely the sum of the first: any two of the five may spend their full margin at once, all five may not. || RENDERER HEADROOM, which is a decision made on E01-M01-S05's behalf. renderer.js is budgeted at 3072 against a measured 1215, leaving 1857 bytes, and S05 is the slice that will fill it. That number is not a forecast of S05 — a virtualised row recycler and a graph canvas will very likely exceed it, and S05 is expected to raise this one budget in a commit that says why and by how much, which is what AGENTS.md section 11 prescribes. The alternative, leaving 8192 so that S05 never has to ask, would hand back the headroom this ratchet was set to protect and would leave the budget unable to see the regression it was just used to find. || WHAT THIS MEASURES, recorded because the number does not show it. Measuring the development build means measuring comment text. The same three bundles built with --production are main.cjs 1078, preload.cjs 547 and renderer.js 649, and almost all of the difference is doc comments, which esbuild strips when it minifies. The consequence is that under this gate a doc comment written in a module a bundle reads spends that bundle's budget. Which of the two builds a size budget should be a budget of is a decision in ADR-0003 section 2, gate 11, and is not settled here; the measurements behind it are in docs/plan/E01-commit-graph/M01-first-graph/S01-scaffold-and-contract.md.
